full_judgment:
6. While the petitioner was discharging its duty, it received a notice issued by said respondent No.3, Member (Customs) dated 9-9-07 to Show cause against the allegations of the Board. In the notice it was alleged amongst others that Messrs Auto Museum Ltd. imported aforesaid five vehicles, namely, Hummer-H3 in connivance with the petitioner company by showing it lower price for which the Government sustained loss of revenue to the tune of Taka 22,87,125.37 against each consignment. It was also asserted that the retail price range of said Hummer-Hi, Model-2006 that was communicated by the Manufacturer was US$ 29,500 to 32,730 excluding tax, licence fee and others charges. Two other PSI Agencies namely, Intertek Testing Services Ltd. and Messrs SGS Bangladesh Ltd. certified the price of such vehicles was US$ 30,415 and 27,053 to 34,541 respectively; and freight charges and charges for conversion of the left hand drive to right hand drive was at US$ 2000 and thereby the value of the jeep came to at US$ 32,215 but the petitioner certified the value at US$ 18,500 and the petitioner thereby helped the importer to evade taxes of said Taka 22,87,125.37. The above activities of the petitioner were violative of section 32 of the Customs Act, 1969 and were punishable for misconduct within the definition of Rule 25(2) clause (3) and Rule 26 of the PSI Rules. 

 12. The petitioner indulged in many cases of misconduct during its tenure as PSI Agency since 6-7-06. Moreover, performance of the petitioner for the services to the Customs authority and the importers were plagued with controversy. Numerous complaints were received from Importer Trade Associations and Chambers and Law Enforcement Agencies with the demand of cancellation of the contracts of the petitioner. The Board also dealt with each and every complaint in accordance with law. During investigation all opportunity was given to the petitioner. Moreover, a notice issued on 3-1-08 under Rule 26 of the PSI Rules for cancellation of the agency of the petitioner for breach of the contract was already served. On 22-1-08 the petitioner appeared therein and submitted his reply to such is notice which is annexed as Annexure- 7. 

 18. Mr Salahuddin Ahmed, learned Additional Attorney-General, submitted that imposition of the penalty by respondent No. 3 who was empowered by column (4) of the Table to sub-rule (2) of rule 25 to impose such penalty for misconduct and loss of revenue under column (2) of said Table was quite valid and lawful and called for no interference. 

 25. In the adjudication order, it was found that the certified value of the vehicles was not correct and that the offence of false declaration in abetting the evasion of revenue was established against the petitioner. Upon such findings, the respondent No.3, Member imposed penalty upon the. petitioner under clause (14) of the Table under section 153(1) read with section 32 of the Customs Act of a sum of Taka 73,89,075.41 and sum of Taka 22,94,043.45 for committing misconduct within the meaning of rule 2 (আ) and (্ঝ) and serial 3 of the Table under rule 25(2) of the PSI Rules.' 

 26. Entire submissions of the learned Advocates centred round the construction of rule 25 of the PSI Rules 2002. Mr Islam did not assail the finding of misconduct as was found by the adjudicating officer. Nor could we find anything on record to help dislodge such finding on misconduct of the petitioner. 

 27. Sub-rule (1), rule 25 of the PSI Rules empowers the Board or any person empowered by such Board to hold an enquiry into the allegations brought against any PSI agency. Rules 2 and 3 empower the persons mentioned in column (4) of the Table to such Rules to impose penalty described in column (2) for misconduct and causing revenue loss as are described against the offence of serial No. 3. Said column (4) of the Table clearly empowers the respondent No. 3, Member to impose the penalty as was imposed. Mr Mahmudul Islam therefore ultimately could not find anything more to challenge the imposition of the penalty under rule 25(2) of the PSI Rules by respondent No.3. 

 32. In any discipline proceeding for misconduct or miss declaration the Board or persons named thereto are given summary power to investigate and punish in summary way following the procedure laid down under rules 25 and 26. When the vires of such rules could not be challenged, the absence of provision for appeal would not make such summary proceeding and adjudication thereon a nullity.
